edges.mechanism: DFMO irreversibly inhibits ODC to deplete polyamines (neuroblastoma maintenance, adenoma chemoprevention); exogenous spermidine directly opposes the therapeutic goal. High dietary polyamine intake abolished DFMO+sulindac adenoma benefit (RR 1.51 top quartile vs 0.19 lower quartiles).
edges.evidence: Secondary analysis of phase III RCT plus mechanism reviews; no direct supplement-drug study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Polyamines are required for tumour growth; tumour-derived spermidine suppresses CD8+ T-cell function and exogenous spermidine accelerated glioblastoma in mice; polyamine depletion is an anticancer strategy. Large cohorts show no increased prostate or colorectal cancer with dietary intake.
edges.evidence: Preclinical and mechanistic reviews; observational human data reassuring but not for supplements in existing cancer; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Above-median dietary polyamine intake associated with higher adenoma recurrence (OR 1.39), but WHI cohort found no increase in colorectal cancer.
edges.evidence: Pooled control arms of 2 RCTs and a large cohort; conflicting; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Renal failure raises plasma putrescine and spermine oxidase activity, producing acrolein (a putative uremic toxin, ~5-fold higher protein-conjugated acrolein); no supplement safety data in CKD.
edges.evidence: Clinical biochemistry studies and reviews; theoretical for supplementation; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Spermidine-rich wheat germ extracts (e.g. spermidineLIFE) contain gluten; synthetic spermidine trihydrochloride or rice germ forms avoid wheat.
edges.evidence: Product labelling and novel-food listing; no clinical reaction reports found

edges.mechanism: Spermidine enhanced anti-PD-L1 efficacy in aged mice, but tumour-derived spermidine acts as a T-cell checkpoint and polyamine synthesis blockade improved anti-PD-1 responses; direction in humans unknown.
edges.evidence: Conflicting preclinical data only; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Dietary spermidine correlated with lower BP in humans and lowered BP in salt-sensitive rats; possible small additive effect.
edges.evidence: Animal data and observational human association; no interaction study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Rapamycin-induced autophagy and longevity require an endogenous spermidine surge with eIF5A hypusination/TFEB; shared autophagy axis.
edges.evidence: Preclinical (yeast, worms, flies, mice); no human combination data

edges.mechanism: Spermidine (acetyltransferase inhibition, SIRT1-independent) and resveratrol (SIRT1 activation) converge on the acetylproteome; synergistic autophagy at subthreshold doses.
edges.evidence: In vitro and model-organism data only

edges.mechanism: Curcumin and spermidine both inhibit EP300 acetyltransferase activity and induce autophagy; potentially additive.
Curcumin (the turmeric constituent) shares EP300 inhibition with spermidine; potentially additive autophagy induction.
edges.evidence: In vitro data only; extrapolated from curcumin

edges.mechanism: Urolithin A drives PINK1/Parkin mitophagy while spermidine drives broader autophagy; proposed complementary use.
Senolytic fisetin and autophagy-inducing spermidine target distinct ageing hallmarks; proposed combined functional food use.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; limited direct evidence for combined use

edges.mechanism: Berberine (AMPK/metabolic) and spermidine (autophagy) target complementary pathways.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; limited direct evidence for combined use

edges.mechanism: Spermidine has been combined with nicotinamide, PEA and OEA in fasting-mimetic products; combination lowered LDL and fasting glucose, but effects cannot be attributed to spermidine. No data for NMN or nicotinamide riboside.
edges.evidence: Small RCT (n=42) and pilot studies of combination products; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Oral spermidine (15 mg/d) raised plasma spermine without changing spermidine; supplementation may confound research biomarkers based on circulating polyamines (MCI/AD, stroke).
ODC1 GG carriers with above-median polyamine intake had higher adenoma odds (OR 1.59); genotype modified eflornithine/sulindac response.
edges.evidence: Secondary analyses of RCT cohorts; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Wheat germ, legumes, nuts, cheese, vegetables and fermented foods contribute dietary spermidine (median ~11.5 mg/d in older CAD patients), comparable to or exceeding supplement doses.
